newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures lose more ground late as longs exit.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures lose more ground late as longs exit.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures continued to lose ground late Thursday in moderate trade, with long liquidation undermining the complex, but some expected the approach of colder weather to soon temper the bears.
At 1430 EDT, November skidded nine cents to $2.38 per million British thermal units. December was 8.9 cents lower at $2.515. 1997 contracts also were down by 1.5 to 7.5 cents.

"There's been a good amount of liquidation by funds and locals, but this market tends to overshoot, and it could be a buy here," said one New York-based futures trader, adding weather, particularly in the Midwest, looked more supportive.

Traders said profit taking after recent gains and selling on bearish AGA data helped pressure the complex at midweek this week, but most expected steady-to-firm cash prices from the upcoming cold to underpin futures near-term. Forecasters expected mostly below-normal Midwest and Northeast temperatures to continue into next week.

Technically, traders pegged support in November in the $2.30 area, with resistance seen at yesterday's high of $2.59 and then in the mid-$2.60s, a measurement objective after the break last week of a head-and-shoulders bottom formation.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices firmed more than five cents Thursday to the high-$2.30s, about 55 cents over October indices. Midcon pipes were steady to up slightly at about the $2.20 level. New York city-gate gas was quoted five cents higher in the mid-$2.60s.
NYMEX said 31,386 Hub contracts traded by 1400 EDT.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas was still down 4.5 cents at $2.07, while deferreds were off similar amounts. NYMEX said 145 Alberta contracts traded by 1400.
NYMEX November Permian natgas was five cents lower at $2.06, while deferreds were untraded. NYMEX said 26 Permian lots traded as of 1400.
On KCBT, November was three cents lower at $2.16, while deferreds were down 4.5 to eight cents. The East/West spread narrowed six cents to 22 cents (NYMEX premium).
